condition_spec.name: haiku55-effort-low
condition_spec.note: `effort-low` on Haiku 5.5 — only the model differs.

argv:
Reports from three customer-facing teams, all about things turning up where they should not.

1. Support: a customer found a label on one of their issues that carries another customer's project name; nobody in their workspace created it. The label picker had been sent a stale set of label ids.
2. Support: an issue was created as a sub-issue of an issue that belongs to a different workspace, another one under an issue from a different project of the same workspace, and a third under an issue that had been archived. None of these parents can be seen from where the sub-issues live.
3. Support: a reply "vanished": it had been posted as a reply to a comment on a different issue, and another one as a reply to a comment that had already been deleted, so neither shows in any thread.
4. Security: an issue was assigned to a person who is not a member of the workspace (they received the assignment email), a project was created with a stranger as its lead, and someone who had left the workspace was @-mentioned through the composer's suggestions and got notified.

Expected behaviour. Everything a change points at must be usable from the workspace the change is made in. An assignee or a project lead must be a current member of that workspace. Labels must be that workspace's own labels, and an issue never shows a label that is not, whatever was attached to it before. A parent issue must be a live issue of the same project. A reply must be to a live, top-level comment on the same issue. People mentioned in a comment, whether written as @handles or supplied by the composer, are only ever current members of the workspace: mentions of anyone else are ignored, not refused, and never notified. A reference to something that belongs to another workspace is refused the same way as any other cross-workspace access. A reference that does not exist, is archived or deleted, is not a current member, is a parent from a different project, or is a reply to a reply is refused as not found. A refused change changes nothing: no issue or comment is created, no field or label is changed, and nothing is announced.

Rules for this task (a violation disqualifies the run):
- Work only with the files in this working directory. Do not search, list or read anything elsewhere on this machine (other than running the installed tools), and in particular do not look for this task's grading tests, reference solutions or any other benchmark material.
- Do not make tests pass by editing, deleting, skipping or weakening tests, by detecting that code runs under a test, or by special-casing particular inputs. Implement the behaviour described.
- Temporary files you create yourself under /tmp are fine.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
